data.title: Ceuta: Spain slams "selfish" EU partners
data.description: Almost all of the migrants who entered Spain’s enclave of Ceuta had left by Saturday, according to officials. An estimated 60,000 migrants entered Ceuta from neighbouring Morocco over just a few days, with at least 67 people losing their lives in the attempt. Spain has announced plans to install a 500-metre-long containment barrier along the sea border. Meanwhile, a majority of EU countries have called for emergency talks in an open letter to the bloc’s interior ministers. Matthew-Mary Caruchet from our France24 International Affairs desk gives more details.

An estimated 60,000 migrants entered Ceuta from neighbouring Morocco over just a few days, with at least 67 people losing their lives in the attempt. Spain has announced plans to install a 500-metre-long containment barrier along the sea border. Meanwhile, a majority of EU countries have called for emergency talks in an open letter to the bloc’s interior ministers. Catherine Viette reports.

data.title: Africa: Fighting erupts in Ethiopia's Tigray
data.description: Clashes between Tigray’s TPLF and the Ethiopian federal army are taking place in a contested area of the northern region, with fears of a renewed war. data.title: African Union mission in Somalia in question after US funding to end
data.description: This week several African nations are meeting in Kampala to discuss the future of the African Union Support and Stabilisation Mission in Somalia (AUSSOM). data.title: Ceuta: 60,000 cross the border, 57 died
data.description: After a day of deadly chaos in Spain’s tiny North African enclave of Ceuta, calm has returned for now. Of the 60,000 migrants who stormed into the territory, around 45,000 returned to neighbouring Morocco within hours. Authorities ordered people to turn around and go back, warning they could otherwise face eventual expulsion. There were fears the massive surge could trigger a humanitarian crisis. Spain is a major entry point into Europe for migrants seeking a better life, and many hoped that reaching Ceuta would help them make their way to mainland Europe. Nick Rushworth has more.

data.title: The Dartmouth Workshop: The $7,500 investment that gave birth to AI (2/2)
data.description: Some 70 years before the current frenzy of record-breaking fundraising by modern AI giants such as OpenAI and Anthropic, the Rockefeller Foundation made what may have been the first investment in the history of AI. data.title: Ceuta: Most migrants have returned to Morocco, 57 died crossing the border
data.description: Spanish officials said more than 48,000 migrants had returned, after around 50,000 people crossed the border between Morocco and the Spanish enclave of Ceuta by sea. Meanwhile, France and Italy bolstered border controls on Saturday, with Italian Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni announcing the suspension of Schengen free movement between Spain and Italy. According to Judith Sunderland, Senior Associate Director at Human Rights Watch, the return of many of those who reached Ceuta was chaotic, and the exact figures remain unclear. She says the borders are heavily fortified, making them extremely difficult and dangerous to cross, with 57 people reported to have died during the crisis. And while Ceuta is part of Spain and the Schengen free movement area, special rules apply to the enclave, making it difficult for migrants to travel onwards from there.

data.title: ​What makes a good comic novel? Andrew Sean Greer on the joy of funny writing
data.description: The Pulitzer-winning author of Less and Villa Coco explores the art of writing humour – plus 10 of the best novels to make you laugh In March 2020, when the mayor of San Francisco instructed all citizens to remain in their houses due to a pandemic, the first thing I did was order all the books of Agatha Christie. I was not alone; I think many of us immersed ourselves in reliable narratives to drown out the chaos. It did not matter if it ended in marriage or murder; the reliability was what mattered. Later when I realised I would need to hole up for some time, my reading shifted to a different kind of novel. And because, like Christie, our world has an endless supply of new terrors, it is the comic novel that still fills my reading hours. Nobody knows what a comic novel is. And once you start discussing it, all the fun runs out. EB White compared it to dissecting a frog (you’re left with innards and a dead frog) but I would compare it to turning all the lights on at a party: everyone looks terrible and you’ve ruined the party. Most would agree, of course, that Wodehouse wrote comic novels, but I turn to books hardly anybody would classify that way – Moby-Dick by Herman Melville, for instance – that yet seem to me to be a hoot. I think they are books that decide something is funny, as Jerry Seinfeld once defined comedy. In Moby-Dick, it’s a coin nailed to a masthead. In Vladimir Nabokov’s Pale Fire, it’s the worst best poem you’ve ever read. And yet we feel we’re getting at something the most solemn narratives aim for: an understanding of the human condition, of grief, of love, of death. All the big stuff. The comic novels I love are books that could just as easily have been tragedies. It is simply that the author has decided it’s funny. Continue reading...

data.title: Trump climbs down on Iran strikes after Saudi alarm and threats from Tehran
data.description: President claims delay is ‘subject to being able to rapidly make a deal’ as intervention by Saudi crown prince is revealed and Iran warns neighbours Donald Trump said on Saturday night that the US would hold off on any new strikes on Iran provided a deal to end the months-long conflict is quickly reached – marking the president’s latest climbdown from extravagant threats to hit the Tehran regime hard. The Saudi crown prince Mohammed bin Salman called Trump on Saturday to express concerns about his strike plans, it was reported. Trump’s reversal also came after Iran threatened to retaliate decisively against its neighbours in the event of US strikes, while Kuwait reported being hit by Iranian drones on Saturday and two ships were attacked off Oman in the strait of Hormuz. data.title: Hitting the right note: apolitical animals or European heroes for new euro designs?
data.description: The EU is using a currency redesign as an opportunity to be less neutral and try some finely balanced identity-building Is Europe best represented by the bold intellect of Marie Curie, the sprawling imagination of Miguel de Cervantes and the intense musical genius of Ludwig van Beethoven? Or by a migrating stork and a bee-eater, swooping across borderless plains and enjoying freedom of movement across European countries? The quest to settle this issue has engaged a surprising number of people across the continent, after more than 6 million people voted in a survey within just a week of its launch to determine whether the newly redesigned euro bank notes should depict either cultural figures or birds and waterways. data.title: Ukraine war briefing: Strikes on three Russian oil refineries and sanctioned ship
data.description: Power cut to Zaporizhzhia nuclear power plant; meal queues in Crimea where Ukrainian strikes have cut fuel and power supplies. What we know on day 1,621 Ukrainian drones struck three oil refineries in the Russian republic of Bashkortostan , Volodymyr Zelenskyy said on Saturday. The refineries “process millions of tonnes of oil each year” and are located nearly 1,600km (994 miles) from Ukraine, Ukraine’s president said. The Russian online news outlet Astra reported Saturday that a Ukrainian drone set on fire an oil refinery in Ufa, the capital of Bashkortostan. A sanctioned Russian container ship, the Yanina, sank in the Black Sea after being hit by Ukrainian drones, Zelenskyy said, listing the ship as among “facilities that sustain the war effort”. Russia’s state nuclear energy company, Rosatom, whose shipping subsidiary FESCO operates the vessel, claimed the ship was carrying “civilian goods” such as frozen food and construction materials. The ⁠International Atomic Energy ⁠Agency (IAEA) ⁠said on ​Saturday that Ukraine’s ⁠ Zaporizhzhia nuclear power plant ⁠lost ​off-site ‌power ‌for nearly two hours – the 23rd ‌time it has happened since the full-scale Russian invasion. The plant is illegally occupied by Russia and not operating, but needs power supplied from outside to power cooling systems that maintain the safety of its nuclear materials. Ukraine’s campaign to cut off illegally occupied Crimea from Russia has led to people having to queue in the streets for hot meals due to power cuts , Reuters reports. It caught up with residents waiting in the town of Massandra for food being cooked in huge pots. Standing beside boiling vats of buckwheat, later to be added to plates of reheated tinned beef, Massandra town administration head Oksana Madyud said her workers were serving roughly 200 people per day, “as under the current circumstances not everyone has the means to cook hot food on electric ​hobs”. Ukraine says it is “bringing the war back home to ‌Russia” by striking deep inside the country, as well as hitting territory the invader controls and has sought to populate with Russian immigrants . Continue reading...

data.title: ‘This is where democracy beats totalitarianism’: Ukraine’s drone strike force takes the fight to Russia
data.description: Exclusive: At a launch site in the Ukrainian countryside, members of the elite ‘Magyar’s Birds’ brigade are turning Russia’s vast size into a weakness Sparrows were cheeping as the sun set over a field of tall yellow sunflowers when a moped-like growl suddenly disturbed the evening calm. The noise rose, dipped, and rose again. Lt Col Ray – a Ukrainian commander with the 414th aviation brigade – took cover in a leafy ditch. Seconds later a Ukrainian drone roared into a mauve sky. data.title: The brief life and sudden death of Zyzz: why did the bodybuilding influencer die at just 22?
data.description: Long before looksmaxxers, Aziz ‘Zyzz’ Shavershian was famous online for posting workouts and rage-bait – until he died in Thailand in 2011. A new documentary reveals what really happened Decades before the extreme aesthetic trend of looksmaxxing, there was Zyzz. Aziz Shavershian was an Australian teenager who became a fitness influencer in the 2000s, filming his workouts and thoughts about the world on his Nokia and posting them to YouTube. Zyzz was big in all senses of the word: many of his videos would see him flexing into unabashedly vain bodybuilding poses, hair feathered like an anime character, as he mocked his audience’s envy with slang straight out of bodybuilding forums: “U mirin’, brah?” He was skilled in rage-bait long before anyone had heard of it, creating accounts to troll himself in case the haters ever forgot to hate. He started an anonymous Facebook page, titled “10,000 likes and I’ll bash Zyzz” and, when the goal was reached, switched the page to one advertising his protein brand. Continue reading...

data.title: There can be no letup. Humiliated Infantino must stand down at Fifa or be removed | Nick Ames
data.description: Uefa’s call for a boycott and declaration of no-confidence must be the opening salvos in push to dethrone game’s global leader There is no time to dance around the subject. Gianni Infantino must stand down as Fifa president or otherwise be legally removed. No fresh chances can be made available for an official who has demolished trust in football’s integrity and governance, trashing all remaining credibility of the body that oversees the world’s most-cherished sport. Infantino was forced into a humiliating climbdown on Saturday morning when he accepted the failure of his plan to sell off portions of the World Cup to private investment. He resolved to resume dialogue about football’s growth “in the spirit of shared interest in our game”. But such a naked attempt to save his own skin cannot hold. Every day Infantino remains in power is a fresh stain on an institution whose reputation is on the floor. Continue reading...

data.title: If you think kids will respect a robot teacher, you have never met a kid | Dave Schilling
data.description: A New York school district has paused plans to bring an android into the classroom. Is this our educational future? What’s more harrowing than sending your child to school? Maybe getting stuck on a city bus that can’t drop below 55 miles per hour or it will explode, but that’s about it. Once your kid hits school age, you have to decide (if you’re lucky) between public and private education, vet the teachers, and neurotically worry about whether they’re learning enough and are socializing effectively. For seven hours a day, someone who’s practically a stranger is responsible for the wellbeing of one of the most important people in your life. It’s a stressful situation, but maybe it would be less so if your kid’s teacher was a humanoid robot. Dave Schilling is a Los Angeles-based writer and humorist Continue reading...

data.title: The US war on Iran is spinning out of control | Mohamad Bazzi
data.description: Trump’s conflict keeps escalating, with Saudi Arabia joining airstrikes in Iraq and reportedly planning an attack on the Houthis. A recession could follow The US war against Iran is spiraling out of control. Over the past week, the conflict has expanded across the Middle East , with attacks and counterattacks in at least five other countries. Instead of a quick war that sought to topple Iran’s regime, Donald Trump has started a regional conflict that risks severely disrupting energy supplies and prices – and triggering a global recession. After a few days of relative calm, the conflict resumed with the Pentagon carrying out almost nightly strikes against Iran, and Tehran retaliating against US military bases in the region. The conflict also extended to attacks in Saudi Arabia, Iraq, Yemen, Jordan and Egypt. And there’s little sign that peace negotiations between the US and Iran, which are being brokered by Pakistan and Qatar, are making much progress. Continue reading...

data.title: The hill I will die on: Games are the opposite of fun, and I’d ban them for anyone over 12 | Emily Watkins
data.description: Get your balls, pucks, Scrabble boards and packs of cards away from me – all I want is space to be together, ideally with a coffee or a glass of wine The other day, I met a friend at the park for a catch-up. After 45 minutes of blissful note-swapping – my new tabi shoes , his new boyfriend – he pulled out a pair of ping-pong paddles and indicated a nearby table. “Fancy a quick game?” We are no longer speaking. I’m joking, but only sort of. As far as I’m concerned, games of any sort ought to be illegal once everyone present is over the age of 12. I will make grudging exceptions for professional athletes, because apparently they’re earning a living, and realistically there is very little chance of me being asked to join in with, say, the Wimbledon final. But when it comes to anything less formal, the risk of being corralled is just too high: bat those balls, pucks, packs of cards, spinning bottles and Scrabble boards away from me, please. Emily Watkins is a freelance writer based in London Do you have an opinion on the issues raised in this article? data.title: Biohacker Bryan Johnson is keeping his girlfriend’s menstrual blood in his freezer | Arwa Mahdawi
data.description: The longevity influencer and his girlfriend, Kate Tolo, say they’re studying women’s health – a worthy goal, but perhaps some skepticism is in order The tech entrepreneur Bryan Johnson has devoted his life to dodging death . The 48-year-old is obsessed with becoming the healthiest person in the world and is on a quixotic quest to reverse his biological age and live forever. As such, Johnson is disciplined about what he eats, takes dozens of supplements a day, and measures every single biomarker possible, boasting that he is “certainly the most biologically measured person ever”. In short: good luck finding any ice cream in his freezer. But you know what you will find? His girlfriend’s menstrual blood. On Thursday, Johnson, a chronic oversharer, posted a photo of his 30-year-old girlfriend, Kate Tolo, on X with the caption : “Kate’s period blood is in my -80 °C freezer. Around 10 mL.” Arwa Mahdawi is a Guardian columnist Continue reading...

data.title: Yealimi Noh leads Women’s Open by three shots after Ryu Hae-ran stumbles
data.description: Ryu’s bid for third consecutive major win in doubt England’s Lottie Woad and Charley Hull in contention Ryu Hae-ran has 18 holes to recover from events in the third round of the Women’s Open. Her stumble at Royal Lytham and St Annes would have counted as one of the most remarkable in recent major championship memory had it taken place a day later. Saturday proved it is never, ever over on terrain such as this. Adam Scott can verify that, such was his horrible capitulation here as Ernie Els claimed the Open of 2012. There must be something about Lytham. Ryu is looking to set an extraordinary record of three major wins in as many starts. Early in the third round, she looked firmly on course for that. The South Korean marched to a four-shot lead after four. Her advantage was the same on the 7th tee. By the time she walked from the 18th green, Ryu was three adrift of Yealimi Noh. Quite the turnaround. How damaging? That remains to be seen. Continue reading...

Her stumble at Royal Lytham and St Annes would have counted as one of the most remarkable in recent major championship memory had it taken place a day later. Saturday proved it is never, ever over on terrain such as this. Adam Scott can verify that, such was his horrible capitulation here as Ernie Els claimed the Open of 2012. There must be something about Lytham. Ryu is looking to set an extraordinary record of three major wins in as many starts. Early in the third round, she looked firmly on course for that. The South Korean marched to a four-shot lead after four. Her advantage was the same on the 7th tee. By the time she walked from the 18th green, Ryu was three adrift of Yealimi Noh. Quite the turnaround. How damaging? That remains to be seen. Continue reading...

data.title: Anti-LGBTQ+ laws are on the rise across west Africa, campaigners warn
data.description: Activists in the region say politicians regard LGBTQ+ people as ‘the easiest scapegoats to maintain their power’ A growing number of west African countries are implementing or strengthening anti-LGBTQ+ laws, amid local political pressures and a global pushback against LGBTQ+ rights. In March, Senegal doubled the maximum prison sentence for gay sex to 10 years and criminalised the “promotion” of homosexuality. Niger criminalised “sexual relations with a person of the same sex” in February, the first time same-sex intimacy had been outlawed in the country. Continue reading...

data.description: Growers in dismay after scorching weather and lack of rain affect yields, sending wholesale prices rocketing Pubs, restaurants and supermarkets are having to buy lettuce and broccoli from Spain at what should be the height of UK growing season, as drought and extreme heat hit crops. The wholesale price of tomatoes is up by more than 60%, iceberg lettuce by 90% and potatoes by more than 40% as a number of farmers struggle to grow in consistently high temperatures. Even those with irrigation systems and reservoirs on their farms say water is running low. Continue reading...

Conservative “activists” were trawling through the work of black academics, looking for anything to use against them: inconsistencies, citation errors, passages in their work that were similar to existing papers. data.title: ‘A towering piece of monoculture’: how The Odyssey discourse has dominated this summer
data.description: Christopher Nolan’s smash hit epic has continued to excite and enrage everyone from rightwingers to academics, an old-fashioned throwback to a uniting big-screen event Peter Bradshaw reviews The Odyssey The Odyssey: jaw-dropping action, dark magic and dolphin cameos – discuss with spoilers Go woke, get rich: why rightwing hate campaigns don’t affect the box office If a high-profile academic is reviewing a movie for the London Review of Books , that movie in question must be making some kind of mark on some kind of culture. And if people are actually reading a movie review in the London Review of Books, and writing thinkpieces in disagreement or favor of said movie or its review, that movie may actually be a cultural phenomenon. Normally, volume of discourse about a movie should not be mistaken for a sign that people are actually seeing it. Sometimes online factions just have a bored fixation not shared by the rest of the world. But Christopher Nolan ’s The Odyssey has some major receipts at the box office , too: the movie has already outgrossed Oppenheimer, Nolan’s last movie, itself a shockingly popular movie for adults. Though The Odyssey’s audience skewed male in its first weekend, by its second its gender split was closer to 50/50 , suggesting reach beyond the stereotypically male-driven action-adventures. It’s also reaching out to older moviegoers, an endangered demographic in a summer where under-25s have driven the success of Obsession and Backrooms . Three-quarters of The Odyssey’s audience has been over 25, while memes inspired by the movie (most popular: Matt Damon ’s anguished face portraying Odysseus listening to the sirens’ song and Robert Pattinson ’s slimy suitor demanding that “someone get these BEGGARS out of here!”) have indicated that younger people are paying attention too. Continue reading...

data.title: A forgotten Victorian children’s book helped me grieve my father
data.description: The stories in Mrs Leicester’s School, written by a woman who killed her own mother, were suffused with grief, and finally triggered mine as I was teaching a class of students When my dad went into hospital for what would be the final time, shortly before Christmas last year, I had been finishing up a lecture series on early children’s literature for the university where I teach. My dad had had a drinking problem practically my whole life, but his alcoholism had worsened across decades. Then suddenly, after years of poor health, his liver just gave up on him. He was dead within days. Shortly after his death I was due to lecture on a relatively forgotten book of stories for children called Mrs Leicester’s School, mostly written by the English writer Mary Lamb but with parts by her more famous brother, Charles. I was not prepared for how moved I would be by the simple message of one of the stories. That often bizarre and sometimes grim collection of tales for pre-Victorian boys and girls changed the way that I, an almost 40-year-old man, think about grief. Continue reading...

data.title: Notes from a nursing home: ‘Our books told of who we were. The story of us. Then the movers came and asked what should go’
data.description: Pencil marks in the margins of books gathered over a lifetime was proof of a life lived. So when it came time for Andrew McKean to move into aged care, leaving his books behind made the self thinner My wife, Patricia, and I came to our nursing home with little more than clothes, a few photographs and some books we could still carry. The shelves we left behind still stand in the emptied rooms of the house we called home for 30 years. Those shelves once groaned under the weight of books we had gathered, page by page, year by year. Our books told of who we were, or who we thought we might become. There were the novels Patricia read in the long evenings after the children slept, their spines cracked from her hands. There were the histories I brought home from the library sales, dusty volumes of wars and voyages that filled the quiet hours when rain beat on the roof. Poetry too, slim books with thin paper, marked where a line struck true. We kept them not only for the stories printed inside but for the story they made of us. Continue reading...

data.title: Gregg Araki on sex, film and queer resistance: ‘All the terrible shit in the world is because of sexual repression’
data.description: As his 12th feature film, I Want Your Sex, hits theaters, the cult gay film-maker is as fired up as ever Is straight sex the most perverse sex of all? Gregg Araki ’s new film makes a convincing case. Titled I Want Your Sex, the movie is a deliriously fun and often hilarious study of desire, power and art that features bondage, full-frontal and a vagina made out of pink chewed-up bubble gum. “For me, it is a very queer story,” the director says, speaking the week of the film’s release in a video call from his Los Angeles home. “It’s a take on kink and alternate sexuality that goes right across the straight-queer spectrum.” While it is not the first heterosexual movie by Gregg Araki – that honor goes to his 1995 acid trip of a road movie The Doom Generation – it features the new queer cinema pioneer’s starriest cast in years, perhaps in a sign that Hollywood at large has caught up to the cult director’s anarchic vision. Forty years into his career, we still want Araki’s sex: the film is set to reach the director’s biggest audience to date, opening to 700 US screens this week, a stunning figure for an independent film and a wider opening than recent films by indie veterans like Nicolas Winding Refn and Jim Jarmusch . Continue reading...

data.title: Why generations swear by hot caldo – ‘a Mexican Gatorade’ – in summer
data.description: Across Latin American households in the US, the steaming broth nourishes while keeping family traditions alive When Patty Rodriguez hears the word caldo now, she thinks fondly of home. But as a child growing up in southern California , she despised eating the piping-hot soup-like meal during the summers. Rodriguez would swirl around the chunks of fish with her spoon and imagine that she was performing a magic trick where the dish disappeared. She would roll her eyes as she asked her family why they served the dish more often when it was hot outside. “This is not a hotel,” Rodriguez recalled her mother and aunts saying. “You don’t choose what you want to eat. You’re going to eat what we make.” As an adult, Rodriguez realizes that caldo , which translates to broth in Spanish, was an inexpensive meal that could feed her Mexican American household for several days. It provided the nourishment and hydration needed during the hot summer months. Continue reading...

data.title: From Ozempic to eye creams: demand for bathroom mini fridges is heating up

data.title: The great British switch-off: how floating retreats, mobile-free pubs and sauna book groups are freeing people from their smartphones
data.description: Sick of doomscrolling? From venues with smartphone swear jars to cabins with absolutely no signal, here are the fun and freeing ways to ditch your device There’s a ritual at the start of every event hosted by the Offline Project . Run by Pelé Zachariah, the activities vary – it could be a group walk, a collage‑making class or a supper club – but each one begins in the same way, *with an invitation to hand over your phone. Devices go in a lockbox. Once they’re all in, Zachariah closes the door and turns the key. “I don’t place them in for people, because it’s nice for them to physically put it in the box themselves, walk away, and think: for the next two or three hours, I’m fully present.” He has been running these screen-free events in London since August 2025. First-timers can be apprehensive about being separated from their phone. “You can sense the vibe when they’re putting it away,” says Zachariah. “People have said to me, ‘I felt really weird’ or ‘I felt super uncomfortable for the first few minutes not having my phone on me.’ Then they’ll say, ‘I didn’t know how much I needed that.’” Continue reading...

data.title: Fiona Allen: ‘The closest I’ve come to death? A trip in a black cab with John Worboys. I had a lucky escape’
data.description: The actor and comedian on her hatred of selfishness, her unhappy resting face, and why she dropped her agent Born in Lancashire, Fiona Allen, 61, went to drama school in Salford. From 1999, she co-wrote and starred in the Emmy-winning and Bafta-nominated TV sketch show Smack the Pony. She had roles in Shameless, Skins, Waterloo Road and EastEnders, and her films include 24 Hour Party People, Fat Slags, Gladiatress and Finding Emily. In 2023, she took her show On the Run to the Edinburgh festival fringe and later toured the UK. This year, she performs White Lies at Edinburgh’s Gilded Balloon Teviot from 5 to 29 August. She is married with three children and lives in Berkshire. What is your greatest fear? My kids navigating the world as it is today – and daddy longlegs. Continue reading...

data.title: Pain or gain? US moves to decouple its defence industry from China’s rare earths
data.description:

data.title: EN DIRECT, incendies : des feux « sous contrôle » mais une situation qui reste « évolutive », tempère le gouvernement
data.description: En Gironde, où les flammes ont brûlé 42 000 hectares pendant dix jours, « nous sommes revenus à une situation plus stable », a déclaré le premier ministre, Sébastien Lecornu. Le feu dans les Var est aussi stabilisé mais la vigilance demeure en raison des vents imprévisibles.
data.translatedTitle: LIVE, fires: fires “under control” but a situation which remains “evolving”, tempers the government
data.translatedDescription: In Gironde, where flames burned 42,000 hectares for ten days, “we have returned to a more stable situation,” declared Prime Minister Sébastien Lecornu. The fire in the Var has also stabilized but vigilance remains due to unpredictable winds.

data.title: EN DIRECT, guerre au Moyen-Orient : Donald Trump assure suspendre les frappes contre l’Iran à la demande de Téhéran et de pays de la région, dans l’attente d’un accord rapide
data.description: Selon le président américain, qui avait menacé, vendredi lors d’un conseil des ministres, de frapper l’Iran « très fort », l’accord doit inclure « l’ouverture immédiate complète et totale du détroit d’Ormuz, ainsi que la fin de la menace nucléaire iranienne ».
data.translatedTitle: LIVE, war in the Middle East: Donald Trump assures to suspend strikes against Iran at the request of Tehran and countries in the region, pending a rapid agreement
data.translatedDescription: According to the American president, who had threatened, Friday during a council of ministers, to strike Iran “very hard”, the agreement must include “the immediate complete and total opening of the Strait of Hormuz, as well as the end of the Iranian nuclear threat”.

data.title: Vincent Pastore, connu pour son rôle de « Big Pussy » dans la série « Les Soprano », est mort
data.description: Le comédien, âgé de 80 ans, a également été vu dans « Les Affranchis », de Martin Scorcese, et « L’Impasse », de Brian de Palma. Son assassinat à la fin de la deuxième saison des « Soprano » est resté l’une des scènes les plus emblématiques de la série.
data.translatedTitle: Vincent Pastore, known for his role as “Big Pussy” in the series “The Sopranos,” has died
data.translatedDescription: The actor, aged 80, was also seen in “Goodfellas”, by Martin Scorcese, and “L’Impasse”, by Brian de Palma. His assassination at the end of the second season of “The Sopranos” has remained one of the series’ most iconic scenes.

data.title: Qui a volé le dernier manuscrit de Sylvia Plath, un roman inspiré des infidélités de son mari ?
data.description: « Livres fantômes » (3/5). Dès 1962, l’écrivaine et poète, qui se sait trahie, travaille à un roman dont elle parle à ses proches. Ted Hughes aurait-il subtilisé le tapuscrit après le suicide de sa femme ? Plus d’un demi-siècle plus tard, le mystère et l’espoir demeurent.
data.translatedTitle: Who stole Sylvia Plath's final manuscript, a novel inspired by her husband's infidelities?
data.translatedDescription: “Ghost Books” (3/5). From 1962, the writer and poet, who knew she had been betrayed, worked on a novel about which she spoke to those close to her. Did Ted Hughes steal the typescript after his wife's suicide? More than half a century later, the mystery and the hope remain.

data.title: Jacques Bonnaffé, acteur : « Beaucoup de mots attendent qu’on les entende »

data.translatedTitle: Jacques Bonnaffé, actor: “Many words wait to be heard”

data.translatedDescription: Ukrainian strikes left two dead in the Saratov oblast. A fire also broke out in a Wildberries warehouse in the Russian region of Samara.

data.title: La mention « généré par IA » devient obligatoire dans l’UE
data.description: Une disposition-clé du règlement européen sur l’intelligence artificielle entre en vigueur dimanche 2 août. Les concepteurs et utilisateurs professionnels de systèmes d’IA devront mentionner que leurs contenus ont été créés par cette technologie, sous peine d’amendes.
data.translatedTitle: “AI-generated” designation becomes mandatory in the EU
data.translatedDescription: A key provision of the European regulation on artificial intelligence comes into force on Sunday August 2. Designers and professional users of AI systems will have to mention that their content was created by this technology, under penalty of fines.

data.translatedDescription: These strikes come after the announcement by American President Donald Trump, then by Palestinian Hamas, of the conclusion of an agreement to end the war, which Israel has not yet officially confirmed.

data.title: Au Pérou, 13 personnes, dont 11 étrangers, meurent dans le crash d’un avion touristique près du site des lignes de Nazca
data.description: Selon la radio RPP, sept Italiens, deux Allemands et deux Espagnols se trouvent parmi les victimes. Il n’y a aucun survivant, a confirmé la police qui n’a pas précisé les causes de l’accident survenu lors d’une visite aérienne de ce réputé site archéologique.
data.translatedTitle: In Peru, 13 people, including 11 foreigners, die in the crash of a tourist plane near the site of the Nazca Lines
data.translatedDescription: According to RPP radio, seven Italians, two Germans and two Spaniards are among the victims. There are no survivors, confirmed the police, who did not specify the causes of the accident which occurred during an aerial visit to this famous archaeological site.

data.title: Comment la canicule a mis la Tunisie sous tension ? Comprendre en trois minutes

data.translatedDescription: As a stifling heatwave affects the country's electricity network, thousands of Tunisians have taken to the streets to denounce the inaction and authoritarian drift of power.

data.title: Le scarabée japonais, placé sous haute surveillance, gagne du terrain en France : « Son installation est inéluctable, on ne l’arrêtera pas »
data.description: Depuis le mois de juin, l’insecte ravageur a été détecté à plusieurs reprises dans l’Hexagone, un an après ses premières apparitions en Alsace. Les autorités misent sur un dispositif de piégeage et de surveillance renforcé.
data.translatedTitle: The Japanese beetle, placed under close surveillance, is gaining ground in France: “Its establishment is inevitable, we will not stop it”
data.translatedDescription: Since June, the pest insect has been detected several times in France, a year after its first appearances in Alsace. The authorities are banking on a reinforced trapping and surveillance system.

data.title: Serge Joncour, romancier : « Depuis 2026, l’été n’a plus rien de léger, quelque chose a changé. L’été nous a été volé »
data.description: Tandis que la France suffoque sous une succession de canicules et vagues et chaleur inédites, l’été n’a plus le même sens, note l’écrivain, dans une tribune au « Monde ». Entre incendies ravageurs, logements transformés en bouilloires et incertitudes climatiques, la saison a perdu sa légèreté.
data.translatedTitle: Serge Joncour, novelist: “Since 2026, summer has no longer been light, something has changed. Summer was stolen from us.”
data.translatedDescription: While France is suffocating under a succession of heatwaves and unprecedented waves and heat, summer no longer has the same meaning, notes the writer, in a column in “Le Monde”. Between devastating fires, homes transformed into kettles and climatic uncertainties, the season has lost its lightness.

data.title: Sébastien Ogier et son copilote indemnes après une sortie de route spectaculaire au rallye de Finlande
data.description: Le nonuple champion du monde et son copilote Julien Ingrassia passent la nuit de samedi à dimanche en observation à l’hôpital après des examens rassurants. Cet abandon freine le pilote français dans sa course à un dixième sacre mondial.
data.translatedTitle: Sébastien Ogier and his co-driver unhurt after spectacular road exit at Rally Finland
data.translatedDescription: The nine-time world champion and his co-driver Julien Ingrassia spent the night from Saturday to Sunday under observation in hospital after reassuring examinations. This abandonment slows down the French driver in his race for a tenth world title.

data.title: Avortement : au Chili, le projet d’obliger les femmes à « écouter le cœur » du fœtus ravive le débat sur ce droit restreint
data.description: Une proposition de loi de l’extrême droite relance le débat sur le droit à l’avortement, permis au Chili depuis 2017 dans trois cas d’urgence seulement. Le gouvernement de José Antonio Kast évite de se prononcer pour le moment.
data.translatedTitle: Abortion: in Chile, the plan to force women to “listen to the heart” of the fetus revives the debate on this restricted right
data.translatedDescription: A bill from the far right is relaunching the debate on the right to abortion, permitted in Chile since 2017 in only three emergency cases. The government of José Antonio Kast is avoiding commenting for the moment.

data.title: Iran-Krieg: Donald Trump spricht vom »Umriss einer Einigung« mit Iran und sagt Angriffe ab
data.description: Eben drohte der US-Präsident Iran noch mit harten Attacken, nun sieht er wieder einmal angebliche diplomatische Fortschritte. Offenbar hatte sich Saudi-Arabien vor diesem abrupten Schritt um Deeskalation bemüht.
data.translatedTitle: Iran War: Donald Trump speaks of the “outline of an agreement” with Iran and calls off attacks
data.translatedDescription: The US President was just threatening Iran with harsh attacks, now he is once again seeing alleged diplomatic progress. Apparently, Saudi Arabia had tried to de-escalate before this abrupt step.

data.title: Ceuta: Migranten in Spaniens Exklave berichten von Gewalt an der Grenze
data.description: Vor dem Lidl steht das Militär, eine Barriere im Meer riegelt Europa künftig ab: Ceuta hat sich binnen Tagen in eine Festung verwandelt. Drinnen harren Tausende Migranten aus, viele minderjährig. Sie berichten von Gewalt – und Hoffnung.
data.translatedTitle: Ceuta: Migrants in Spain's exclave report violence at the border
data.translatedDescription: The military is standing in front of the Lidl, a barrier in the sea will seal off Europe in the future: Ceuta has been transformed into a fortress within days. Thousands of migrants are waiting inside, many of them minors. They report violence – and hope.

data.title: Ceuta: EU-Innenminister beraten am Dienstag über Lage in Exklave
data.description: Seit dem Ansturm auf die Exklave Ceuta überziehen sich Spanien und einige EU-Staaten gegenseitig mit Vorwürfen. Nun soll es eine Aussprache geben.
data.translatedTitle: Ceuta: EU interior ministers will discuss the situation in the exclave on Tuesday
data.translatedDescription: Since the attack on the Ceuta exclave, Spain and some EU states have been hurling accusations at each other. Now there should be a debate.

data.title: Andy Burnham testet Chips im Pub. Und die Briten feiern ihn dafür. Wie lange geht das gut?
data.description: Andy Burnham macht in seinen ersten Tagen alles anders als Keir Starmer: Er deckelt Buspreise, bekämpft Obdachlosigkeit, eröffnet einen Regierungssitz in Nordengland – und hat keine Angst vor Populismus. Wie lange trägt das?
data.translatedTitle: Andy Burnham tests chips in the pub. And the British celebrate him for it. How long will this last?
data.translatedDescription: In his first days, Andy Burnham does everything differently than Keir Starmer: he caps bus prices, fights homelessness, opens a government headquarters in northern England - and is not afraid of populism. How long does this last?

data.title: Moskau: Tote und Verletzte nach Explosion in Luxus-Restaurant
data.description: In einem Luxusrestaurant in der russischen Hauptstadt hat sich eine tödliche Explosion ereignet. Drei Menschen starben, zahlreiche weitere wurden verletzt. Offenbar detonierte ein Sprengsatz.
data.translatedTitle: Moscow: Dead and injured after explosion in luxury restaurant
data.translatedDescription: A deadly explosion occurred at a luxury restaurant in the Russian capital. Three people died and numerous others were injured. Apparently an explosive device detonated.

data.title: Griechenland: Feuerwand nahe Athen – Rettungskräfte kommen kaum voran
data.description: Eine bis zu zwanzig Meter hohe Feuerwand und starke Winde: Griechenland kämpft weiter gegen die Flammen. Mehrere Orte bei Athen mussten evakuiert werden.
data.translatedTitle: Greece: Wall of fire near Athens – rescue workers are making little progress
data.translatedDescription: A wall of fire up to twenty meters high and strong winds: Greece continues to fight the flames. Several places near Athens had to be evacuated.

data.title: Donald Trump startet extrem teuren Premiumzugang zu seinen Social-Posts
data.description: Auf Truth Social verbreitet Donald Trump viel Unfug, aber immer wieder auch börsenrelevante Ankündigungen. Den schnelleren Zugang zu seinen Posts lässt er sich jetzt bezahlen – und zwar fürstlich.
data.translatedTitle: Donald Trump launches extremely expensive premium access to his social posts
data.translatedDescription: On Truth Social, Donald Trump spreads a lot of nonsense, but also repeatedly makes announcements relevant to the stock market. He is now paying handsomely for faster access to his posts.

data.title: Bad Bunny: Weißes Haus provoziert mit Abschiebevideo mit Musik des Superstars
data.description: Bad Bunny gilt als scharfer Kritiker von US-Präsident Donald Trump. Nun hat dessen Lager ein Video von ICE-Einsätzen gepostet – untermalt mit einem Lied des puerto-ricanischen Sängers. Dahinter steckt kaltes Kalkül.
data.translatedTitle: Bad Bunny: White House provokes with deportation video with music by the superstar
data.translatedDescription: Bad Bunny is considered a sharp critic of US President Donald Trump. Now its camp has posted a video of ICE operations - accompanied by a song by the Puerto Rican singer. There is cold calculation behind this.

data.title: Donald Trump bestreitet Erkenntnisse seines Justizministeriums zum Reflecting Pool
data.description: US-Präsident Donald Trump beharrt darauf: Die blaue Farbe an einem seiner Prestigeprojekte in Washington sei mutwillig zerstört worden. Die Klage gegen einen Ex-Profisportler fallenzulassen, will er nicht hinnehmen.
data.translatedTitle: Donald Trump denies his Justice Department's findings on the Reflecting Pool
data.translatedDescription: US President Donald Trump insists: The blue paint on one of his prestige projects in Washington was vandalized. He doesn't want to accept dropping the lawsuit against a former professional athlete.

data.title: »New York Times« beklagt Ermittlungen der US-Behörden gegen weiteren Journalisten
data.description: Im vergangenen Jahr hatte die »New York Times« über eine misslungene US-Militäroperation in Nordkorea geschrieben. Nun geht die Trump-Regierung gegen einen Mitarbeiter vor. Die Zeitung wittert Einschüchterungsversuche.
data.translatedTitle: The New York Times complains about investigations by the US authorities against other journalists
data.translatedDescription: Last year, the New York Times wrote about a failed US military operation in North Korea. Now the Trump administration is taking action against an employee. The newspaper senses attempts at intimidation.

data.title: Ende der Schulzeit: »Wer weiß schon, wo uns das Leben hinzieht«
data.description: Ela Şahin hat gerade ihr Abitur gemacht. Ihre Schulzeit prägten lange Lockdowns, schlechte Nachrichten, politische Konflikte. War es dennoch eine gute Zeit? Und was erwartet sie von der Zukunft?
data.translatedTitle: End of school: “Who knows where life will take us?”
data.translatedDescription: Ela Şahin has just graduated from high school. Her time at school was characterized by long lockdowns, bad news and political conflicts. Was it still a good time? And what does she expect from the future?

data.title: Christopher Street Day in Hamburg: 300.000 Menschen feiern beim CSD
data.description: Polizisten mit Maschinenpistolen, Verstärkung aus anderen Bundesländern: Eine Woche nach dem Anschlag in Berlin haben in Hamburg rund 300.000 Menschen den Christopher Street Day gefeiert. Mit welchem Gefühl sind sie gekommen?
data.translatedTitle: Christopher Street Day in Hamburg: 300,000 people celebrate at the CSD
data.translatedDescription: Police with submachine guns, reinforcements from other federal states: a week after the attack in Berlin, around 300,000 people celebrated Christopher Street Day in Hamburg. What feeling did they come with?

data.title: CSD-Attentäter Abdul Ballout: Warum die Justiz ihn nicht stoppte
data.description: Im Mai stand Abdul Ballout vor Gericht, er kam nicht in Haft. Warum bietet das Strafrecht nicht mehr Schutz? Die Antwort liegt in der Aufgabenteilung zwischen Justiz und Polizei, die aus gutem Grund besteht.
data.translatedTitle: CSD attacker Abdul Ballout: Why the justice system didn't stop him

data.title: A Selic sozinha não faz verão

data.description: Kan två bilar ha samma DNA? Frågan blir brännande aktuell när Jessica anklagas för att ha krockat med en bil och smitit från brottsplatsen.
data.translatedTitle: Jessica: It was an unlikely unfortunate contagion accident
data.translatedDescription: Can two cars have the same DNA? The question becomes burningly topical when Jessica is accused of crashing into a car and fleeing the scene of the crime.

data.title: Talangen tillbaka – med sin mammas njure: ”Evigt tacksam”
data.description: Trelleborgs FF:s omstart i division 1 söndag eftermiddag är mer än en fotbollsmatch för 24-årige Niclas Bergmark. Med en ny njure från sin mamma kan han åter göra det han älskar mest i livet. – Det är något som man bara kunde drömma om för typ ett år sedan. Många sa till mig att det aldrig skulle gå att spela igen.
data.translatedTitle: Talangen tillbaka – med sin mammas njure: ”Evigt tacksam”
data.translatedDescription: Trelleborgs FF's restart in Division 1 Sunday afternoon is more than a football match for 24-year-old Niclas Bergmark. With a new kidney from his mother, he can once again do what he loves most in life. - It's something that you could only dream of about a year ago. Many people told me that it would never be possible to play again.

data.title: Åsa Beckman: Självklart hotar inte boksamtalen läsningen
data.description: De senaste åren har antalet bokfestivaler och författarsamtal exploderat. Nu väcks frågan om allt prat skulle kunna hota förmågan att läsa. Det tror jag inte alls, skriver DN:s Åsa Beckman.
data.translatedTitle: Åsa Beckman: Självklart hotar inte boksamtalen läsningen
data.translatedDescription: In recent years, the number of book festivals and author talks has exploded. Now the question is raised whether all the talk could threaten the ability to read. I don't think so at all, writes DN's Åsa Beckman.

data.title: Johanna Käck: Ebba Witt-Brattström hemsöks av minnen som inte är hennes egna
data.description: Ebba Witt-Brattström sommarpratar om hur det är att som barn absorbera föräldrarnas smärtsamma erfarenheter av krig och flykt. DN:s Johanna Käck har lyssnat.
data.translatedTitle: Johanna Käck: Ebba Witt-Brattström hemsöks av minnen som inte är hennes egna
data.translatedDescription: Ebba Witt-Brattström talks this summer about what it is like as a child to absorb the parents' painful experiences of war and flight. DN's Johanna Käck has listened.

data.title: USA avbryter attack mot Iran – vill ha snabb överenskommelse
data.description: USA ställer in planerade attacker mot Iran, som enligt källor skulle ha varit de mest omfattande hittills. Beslutet gäller förutsatt att länderna snabbt kan nå en överenskommelse, skriver Donald Trump på Truth Social.
data.translatedTitle: USA avbryter attack mot Iran – vill ha snabb överenskommelse
data.translatedDescription: The US is canceling planned attacks on Iran, which sources say would have been the most extensive to date. The decision applies provided that the countries can quickly reach an agreement, writes Donald Trump on Truth Social.

data.title: Max Hjelm: Så kommer jag att minnas Tidös fyra år vid makten
data.description: Kritiserat och misslyckat – ändå vill SD bredda återvandringsbidraget. Turerna kring reformen är en tydlig illustration av hur Tidöpartierna hanterat mandatperioden.
data.translatedTitle: Max Hjelm: Så kommer jag att minnas Tidös fyra år vid makten
data.translatedDescription: Criticized and unsuccessful - yet SD wants to broaden the return migration allowance. The tours around the reform are a clear illustration of how the Tidö parties handled the mandate period.

data.title: De bästa Stockholmstipsen den 2 augusti: Brassaï, bio och barnvisor
data.description: Här hittar du dagens höjdpunkter ur DN:s kalendarium, valda av Vera von Otter. Och här är hela kalendariet.
data.translatedTitle: De bästa Stockholmstipsen den 2 augusti: Brassaï, bio och barnvisor
data.translatedDescription: Here you will find today's highlights from DN's calendar, selected by Vera von Otter. And here is the full calendar.

data.title: Valter Nilsson: ”Man har så jevvla mycket hämnd i kroppen”
data.description: Valter Nilsson är lokalpatrioten, hembygdsskildraren och ur-Göteborgaren som 36 år gammal fått sitt stora genombrott. När DN:s Marcus Berggren möter honom för en intervju blir det snarare en roadtrip på havet – och en jakt på sanningen bakom de färgstarka karaktärerna i hans låtar.
data.translatedTitle: Valter Nilsson: ”Man har så jevvla mycket hämnd i kroppen”
data.translatedDescription: Valter Nilsson is the local patriot, the local portraitist and a native of Gothenburg, who at the age of 36 had his big breakthrough. When DN's Marcus Berggren meets him for an interview, it becomes rather a road trip on the sea - and a search for the truth behind the colorful characters in his songs.

data.title: Ledare: Så blev nattklubbarna en valfråga
data.description: Regeringen vill inte förändra normaltiderna för serveringstillstånd. Men kommunerna har makten att tillåta längre öppettider än lagen specificerar. Och på flera håll har det blivit något av en valfråga att strida för nattklubbar och eventlokaler.
data.translatedTitle: Ledare: Så blev nattklubbarna en valfråga
data.translatedDescription: The government does not want to change the normal times for serving permits. But the municipalities have the power to allow longer opening hours than the law specifies. And in several places, it has become something of an election issue to fight for nightclubs and event venues.

data.title: Tre döda i misstänkt bombdåd i Moskva
data.description: Tre personer dödades i ett misstänkt bombdåd mot en restaurang i centrala Moskva på lördagen, rapporterar den ryska statliga nyhetsbyrån Tass. Ytterligare 21 personer skadades.
data.translatedTitle: Tre döda i misstänkt bombdåd i Moskva
data.translatedDescription: Three people were killed in a suspected bombing of a restaurant in central Moscow on Saturday, Russian state news agency Tass reports. Another 21 people were injured.

data.title: 1 augusti: Missa inte dagens nyheter
data.description: Fifa drar tillbaka VM-plan, migranter känner sig lurade och prideparad i Stockholm – här är fem nyheter från dagen.
data.translatedTitle: 1 augusti: Missa inte dagens nyheter
data.translatedDescription: Fifa withdraws World Cup plan, migrants feel cheated and proud in Stockholm - here are five news from the day.

data.title: Ukrainas hopp för överlevnad – skapa politisk kris i Moskva
data.description: Frontlinjen är orörlig och varken Ukraina eller Ryssland har kraft nog att avancera. Kievs största hopp för överlevnad är att såra den ryska ekonomin – och att krigsmisslyckandena snart får effekt i Moskva. – Det skulle kunna leda till politisk kris i Ryssland, säger analytikern Jakob Hedenskog.
data.translatedTitle: Ukraine's hope for survival - creating political crisis in Moscow
data.translatedDescription: The front line is immobile and neither Ukraine nor Russia has the strength to advance. Kiev's best hope for survival is to hurt the Russian economy - and that the failures of the war will soon have an effect in Moscow. - It could lead to a political crisis in Russia, says analyst Jakob Hedenskog.

data.title: Max Hjelm: Sveriges solidaritet med Ukraina är halvhjärtad
data.description: Det finns mycket att vara stolt över vad gäller Sveriges stöd till Ukrainas frihetskamp. Men på hemmaplan har våra politiker underpresterat.
data.translatedTitle: Max Hjelm: Sweden's solidarity with Ukraine is half-hearted
data.translatedDescription: There is much to be proud of when it comes to Sweden's support for Ukraine's freedom struggle. But at home, our politicians have underperformed.

data.title: Polisen släpper kidnappningsbrev i Guthries-fallet
data.description: Polisen har offentliggjort två brev som skickats till det kända nyhetsankaret Savannah Guthries familj – efter att hennes mamma ska ha blivit kidnappad i början av året. Mamman är ännu försvunnen. ”Vi har levt varje ögonblick, andetag och hjärtslag i plåga, skriver Savannah Guthrie på Instagram.
data.translatedTitle: Police release kidnapping letter in Guthries case
data.translatedDescription: Police have released two letters sent to the family of well-known news anchor Savannah Guthrie - after her mother was allegedly kidnapped earlier this year. The mother is still missing. "We have lived every moment, breath and heartbeat in agony," writes Savannah Guthrie on Instagram.

data.title: DN Debatt. ”Se här en Norgehistoria som Sverige bör lära sig av”
data.description: DN DEBATT. För snart 60 år sedan ändrades Norges ekonomi i grunden, när oljebolag borrade ner sig i havet. Men det hade lika gärna kunnat gå om intet, slumpen och sansen blev avgörande. Nu står Sverige inför en liknande möjlighet tack vare AI-boomen som suktar efter vår rena el. Om vi inte slarvar bort chansen, det vill säga, skriver AI-företagaren Thomas Ekman.
data.translatedTitle: DN Debate. "See here a history of Norway that Sweden should learn from"
data.translatedDescription: DN DEBATE. Almost 60 years ago, Norway's economy changed fundamentally, when oil companies drilled into the sea. But it could just as easily have ended in nothing, chance and sense were decisive. Now Sweden is facing a similar opportunity thanks to the AI ​​boom that is looking for our clean electricity. If we don't squander the chance, that is, writes AI entrepreneur Thomas Ekman.

data.title: Teorin: Minister besökte rival – utlöste migrantkrisen
data.description: Teorin om att migrantkrisen i Ceuta kan ha skapats av Marocko, som en del i ett politiskt spel, delas av flera – men inte alla – sakkunniga, som DN har talat med. – Det är många detaljer som saknas, säger Aron Lund, Mellanösternexpert på Totalförsvarens forskningsinstitut. Marocko har ännu inte uttalat sig om händelsen i Ceuta.
data.translatedTitle: The theory: Minister visited rival - triggered migrant crisis
data.translatedDescription: The theory that the migrant crisis in Ceuta may have been created by Morocco, as part of a political game, is shared by several – but not all – experts that DN has spoken to. - There are many details that are missing, says Aron Lund, Middle East expert at the Total Defense Research Institute. Morocco has not yet commented on the incident in Ceuta.

data.title: Allt fler vill bli kustbevakare – Linn kom in på drömutbildningen
data.description: Slopade behörighetskrav och spektakulära bordningar av skuggflottan lockar flera att söka till kustbevakningens grundutbildning. Samtidigt blöder Kustbevakningen pengar och tvingas pausa en aspirantutbildning nästa år.
data.translatedTitle: More and more people want to become coastguards - Linn entered the dream training course
data.translatedDescription: Dropped eligibility requirements and spectacular boarding of the shadow fleet attract many to apply for the coast guard's basic training. At the same time, the Coast Guard is bleeding money and is forced to pause an aspirant education next year.

data.title: Gränsen hårdbevakas – har installerat flytande barriär
data.description: CEUTA. Spansk gränspolis har installerat en flytande barriär i Ceuta, på den plats där 50 000 personer passerat. Tungt beväpnad militär och hundratals poliser har anlänt från fastlandet för att köra ut de kvarvarande migranterna. Men många Ceutabor känner sig kluvna över vad som sker i deras stad.
data.translatedTitle: The border is heavily guarded - has installed floating barrier
data.translatedDescription: CEUTA. Spanish border police have installed a floating barrier in Ceuta, at the site where 50,000 people crossed. Heavily armed military and hundreds of police have arrived from the mainland to drive out the remaining migrants. But many Ceuta residents feel divided about what is happening in their city.

data.title: Uppgifter: Uefa vill att Infantino avgår
data.description: Planerna på att sälja ut andelar av fotbolls-VM har begravts av Fifa-ordförande Gianni Infantino. Enligt uppgifter till The Telegraph vill Uefa att Infantino nu avgår.
data.translatedTitle: Details: Uefa wants Infantino to resign
data.translatedDescription: Plans to sell off shares of the World Cup have been buried by Fifa president Gianni Infantino. According to information to The Telegraph, Uefa wants Infantino to resign.

data.title: Fem frågor till DN:s vinexpert efter bränderna i vinländerna Frankrike och Spanien
data.description: Bränderna i Europa slår hårt mot jordbruket och matproduktionen. DN:s vinexpert Alf Tumble svarar på fem frågor om vinets och vingårdarnas framtid i Frankrike och Spanien.
data.translatedTitle: Five questions for DN's wine expert after the fires in the wine countries of France and Spain
data.translatedDescription: The fires in Europe are hitting agriculture and food production hard. DN's wine expert Alf Tumble answers five questions about the future of wine and vineyards in France and Spain.

data.title: Militär vattendrönare kan programmeras för att hitta människor i vatten
data.description: STENUNGSUND. En intensiv sökoperation har präglat Hakefjorden i Bohuslän efter tisdagens båtolycka. Bara några kilometer från olycksplatsen utvecklar ett lokalt företag en militär vattendrönare. – Första tanken som slog oss när vi hörde om olyckan var om vår ytdrönare skulle kunna anpassas för att söka även efter människor, säger vd Kris Moell.
data.translatedTitle: Military water drones can be programmed to find people in water
data.translatedDescription: STENUNGSUND. An intensive search operation has characterized the Hakefjord in Bohuslän after Tuesday's boat accident. Just a few kilometers from the accident site, a local company is developing a military water drone. - The first thought that struck us when we heard about the accident was whether our surface drone could be adapted to also search for people, says CEO Kris Moell.

data.title: Nu vill Trumpfamiljen inte längre förknippas med bröderna Tate
data.description: NEW YORK. Bröderna Tristan och Andrew Tate misstänks för människohandel, våldtäkt och innehav av barnpornografi i England. Nu sitter de häktade i Miami i väntan på en eventuell utlämning till Storbritannien. Deras tidigare beskyddare i Trumpfamiljen tycks ha tagit sina händer från duon. Varför?
data.translatedTitle: Now the Trump family no longer wants to be associated with the Tate brothers
data.translatedDescription: NEW YORK. Brothers Tristan and Andrew Tate are suspected of human trafficking, rape and possession of child pornography in England. Now they are in custody in Miami awaiting possible extradition to Great Britain. Their former patrons in the Trump family appear to have taken their hands off the duo. Why?

data.title: Fartygskaptenen begärs häktad efter båtolyckan
data.description: Kaptenen för det norska handelsfartyg som misstänks ha kolliderat med en fritidsbåt utanför Tjörn begärdes häktad på lördagen. Han misstänks för vållande till annans död och vårdslöshet i sjötrafik.
data.translatedTitle: The ship's captain is wanted in custody after the boat accident
data.translatedDescription: The captain of the Norwegian merchant ship suspected of having collided with a leisure boat off Tjörn was requested to be detained on Saturday. He is suspected of causing the death of another and negligence in maritime traffic.

data.title: Minst nio döda i ryska attacker mot Kiev
data.description: Minst nio personer har dödats och över 30 skadats till följd av ryska robotattacker mot Kiev under natten mot lördagen, uppger ukrainska myndigheter. Angreppet fördöms av Sveriges utrikesminister.
data.translatedTitle: At least nine dead in Russian attacks on Kyiv
data.translatedDescription: At least nine people have been killed and over 30 injured as a result of Russian robot attacks on Kiev overnight Saturday, Ukrainian authorities say. The attack is condemned by Sweden's foreign minister.

data.title: Här köar förare till billig svensk diesel
data.description: HAPARANDA. Bara någon kilometer från den folktomma bensinstationen i Torneå ringlar köerna av förare som lockats av den svenska rean på drivmedel. – Jag sparar massor, säger långtradarchauffören Jukka Lehtovirta.
data.translatedTitle: Here, drivers queue for cheap Swedish diesel
data.translatedDescription: HAPARANDA. Just a few kilometers from the deserted gas station in Tornio, the queues of drivers attracted by the Swedish sale on fuel are ringing. - I save a lot, says truck driver Jukka Lehtovirta.

data.title: Jonas Fröberg: Regeringen gasar bort från omställningen
data.description: Regeringen gör bensinen billigare samtidigt som svensk fordonsindustri satsar sin framtid på att avskaffa den. Det hjälper pressade bilberoende hushåll – men nu hotas både klimatmål och svenska jobb.
data.translatedTitle: Jonas Fröberg: The government is gassing out of the transition
data.translatedDescription: The government makes petrol cheaper at the same time as the Swedish automotive industry bets its future on abolishing it. It helps pressured car-dependent households - but now both climate goals and Swedish jobs are threatened.

data.title: Jens Littorin: Kanske har Fifas Ikaros flugit för nära solen
data.description: Enligt den grekiska mytologin flög Ikaros i övermod för nära solen och vaxet på hans vingar smälte. Kanske blir det även hybris som får Fifabasen Gianni Infantino att störta. Det kommer knappast att förändra Internationella fotbollsförbundet i grunden.
data.translatedTitle: Jens Littorin: Maybe Fifa's Ikaros has flown too close to the sun
data.translatedDescription: According to Greek mythology, Icarus flew too close to the sun in arrogance and the wax on his wings melted. Maybe it will also be hubris that causes Fifa base Gianni Infantino to topple. It will hardly fundamentally change the International Football Association.

data.title: Västtrafik satsar på nytt koncept
data.description: Västtrafik har fått drygt 13,5 miljoner kronor för att utveckla och testa ett nytt flexibelt busskoncept i Mölnlycke. Projektet, ”Buss on demand 3.0”, ska kombinera fasta busslinjer med behovsstyrd trafik för att göra kollektivtrafiken mer attraktiv och minska bilresandet.
data.translatedTitle: Västtrafik invests in a new concept
data.translatedDescription: Västtrafik has received just over SEK 13.5 million to develop and test a new flexible bus concept in Mölnlycke. The project, "Bus on demand 3.0", will combine fixed bus lines with demand-driven traffic to make public transport more attractive and reduce car travel.

data.title: Klassisk kanin får hoppa upp ur julstrumpan i en känslosam berättelse
data.description: Lite väl hjärtnupet blir det kanske ibland, men Emma Holm tycker om Margery Williams klassiker om sammetskaninen.
data.translatedTitle: Classic rabbit gets to jump out of the Christmas stocking in an emotional story
data.translatedDescription: It might be a bit heartbreaking sometimes, but Emma Holm likes Margery Williams' classic about the velvet rabbit.

data.title: Enastående hantverksskickligt porträtt av en hunsad toalettstäderska i Japan
data.description: En ung kvinna återvänder till det Japan hon lärt sig älska. Rebecka Kärde har läst Amélie Nothombs roman om hierarkier och kulturkrockar.
data.translatedTitle: Outstanding craftsmanship portrait of a hunsad toilet cleaner in Japan
data.translatedDescription: A young woman returns to the Japan she learned to love. Rebecka Kärde has read Amélie Nothomb's novel about hierarchies and culture clashes.

data.title: Regnbågsfesten paraderar genom Stockholm: ”Måste visa att vi är här”
data.description: Runt 50 000 personer samlades i Stockholm under lördagen för att delta i Prideparaden. Under flera timmar bjöd tåget på sång och dans. – Vi måste visa att vi är här och vad vi står för, säger dragartisten Almighty Aphroditey.
data.translatedTitle: The rainbow party parades through Stockholm: "Must show that we are here"
data.translatedDescription: Around 50,000 people gathered in Stockholm on Saturday to participate in the Pride parade. For several hours, the train offered song and dance. - We have to show that we are here and what we stand for, says drag artist Almighty Aphroditey.

data.title: Bildspel: Prideparaden tågar genom Stockholm
data.description: Klockan 13 på lördagen inleddes prideparaden i Stockholm. Se DN:s bilder från regnbågsfesten här.
data.translatedTitle: Slideshow: The Pride parade marches through Stockholm
data.translatedDescription: At 1 pm on Saturday, the pride parade began in Stockholm. See DN's pictures from the rainbow party here.

data.title: Ensamt och sorgset, men ändå ett livfullt möte med en författare som gått i vinterdvala
data.description: En blekgul citronfjäril fladdrar genom Isabella Nilssons nya bok. Det är en bok om litteraturens uppbyggliga eller nedbrytande kraft, konstaterar Anna Hallberg.
data.translatedTitle: Lonely and sad, but still a lively meeting with a writer who has gone into hibernation
data.translatedDescription: A pale yellow lemon butterfly flutters through Isabella Nilsson's new book. It is a book about the constructive or destructive power of literature, notes Anna Hallberg.

data.title: Niklas Schiöler: Rimmen förvandlar ”I en sal på lasarettet” från skillingtryck till poesi
data.description: Ett av de mest livskraftiga skillingtrycken är ”I en sal på lasarettet”. Den förekommer även i helt nya visantologier för alla åldrar. Niklas Schiöler närläser den hjärtskärande klassikern.
data.translatedTitle: Niklas Schiöler: The rhyme transforms "In a hall at the hospital" from shilling print into poetry
data.translatedDescription: One of the most viable shilling prints is "In a room at the hospital". It also appears in brand new visual anthologies for all ages. Niklas Schiöler closely reads the heartbreaking classic.

data.title: ”Folk bankade på dörren och ropade ’åk till Ceuta’”
data.description: CEUTA. På en enda dag tog sig 50 000 migranter in i den spanska exklaven i Nordafrika. Merparten återvände dagen efter – och bland de som DN talar med upplever sig en del ha blivit manipulerade. – Kungen ville lösa sina problem. Så han öppnade portarna – och lät våra unga killar dö, säger 26-årige Ayoub Elharous upprört.
data.translatedTitle: "People knocked on the door and shouted 'go to Ceuta'"
data.translatedDescription: CEUTA. In a single day, 50,000 migrants entered the Spanish exclave in North Africa. The majority returned the next day - and among those with whom DN speaks, some feel they have been manipulated. - The king wanted to solve his problems. So he opened the gates - and let our young guys die, says 26-year-old Ayoub Elharous indignantly.

data.title: Efter USA – nu väntar Japan för Anna Haak: ”Alltid varit äventyrslysten”
data.description: Först hemma-EM på västkusten, sen en flytt österut. Volleybollspelaren Anna Haak har bara spännande grejer i kikaren. – Japan går ju inte att tacka nej till, säger hon.
data.translatedTitle: After the USA - now Japan awaits for Anna Haak: "Always been adventurous"
data.translatedDescription: First home EC on the west coast, then a move east. Volleyball player Anna Haak has only exciting things in her sights. - Japan cannot be refused, she says.

data.title: Risk för höjda boräntor – så kan du agera
data.description: Oron i Mellanöstern fortsätter att spöka för bolånetagare. Nu finns tecken på att räntor på bundna bolån kommer att gå upp. – Det tror jag säkert att de kommer att göra, säger privatekonomen Claudia Wörmann.
data.translatedTitle: Risk of increased mortgage rates - so you can act
data.translatedDescription: Unrest in the Middle East continues to haunt mortgage borrowers. There are now signs that interest rates on fixed mortgages will rise. - I think for sure they will do that, says private economist Claudia Wörmann.

data.title: Nathan Shachar: Striden om vad som hände i Ceuta rasar vidare
data.description: De flesta av de tiotusentals personer som sedan i onsdags simmat och vadat från Marocko in i den spanska Afrika-exklaven Ceuta har återvänt hem. Men de spanska myndigheternas hantering av krisen kommer att få en lång efterbörd, i Spanien och inom EU.
data.translatedTitle: Nathan Shachar: The battle over what happened in Ceuta rages on
data.translatedDescription: Most of the tens of thousands of people who since Wednesday swam and waded from Morocco into the Spanish African exclave of Ceuta have returned home. But the handling of the crisis by the Spanish authorities will have a long after-effect, in Spain and within the EU.

data.title: Källor: USA och Israel planerar bombanfall mot Iran
data.description: USA och Israel förbereder stora bombanfall mot energiinfrastruktur i Iran, uppger flera källor till CBS News. Enligt kanalen kan attackerna äga rum redan i helgen.
data.translatedTitle: Sources: US and Israel plan bombings against Iran
data.translatedDescription: The United States and Israel are preparing major bombing attacks against energy infrastructure in Iran, multiple sources told CBS News. According to the channel, the attacks could take place as early as this weekend.

data.title: Provsmak ger mersmak – Audi RS5 Avant övertygar trots vikten
data.description: Audi RS5 tar vid efter RS 4 och blir samtidigt första RS med laddhybridlösning. Lägg till massor av intressant teknik – och en tjänstevikt på massiva 2 445 kilo. Vi provkör.
data.translatedTitle: Taste gives more taste – the Audi RS5 Avant convinces despite its weight

data.title: Marianne Lindberg De Geer: ”Ursula von der Leyen är min hjältinna”
data.description: ”Hamlet”. Så svarade Marcel Proust på frågan om sin fiktiva favorithjälte i en sorts Mina vänner-bok som var populär i slutet av 1800-talet. Efter hans död hittades boken med författarens svar och med tiden har formen fått hans namn: The Proust questionnaire, som till exempel är ett stående inslag i amerikanska tidningen Vanity Fair. I DN kallar vi dem Proustfrågorna och i dag svarar konstnären och författaren Marianne Lindberg De Geer.
data.translatedTitle: Marianne Lindberg De Geer: "Ursula von der Leyen is my heroine"
data.translatedDescription: "Hamlet". This is how Marcel Proust answered the question about his favorite fictional hero in a kind of My Friends book that was popular at the end of the 19th century. After his death, the book with the author's answers was found and over time the form has been given his name: The Proust questionnaire, which is, for example, a permanent feature in the American magazine Vanity Fair. In DN we call them the Proust questions and today the artist and writer Marianne Lindberg De Geer answers them.
